correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), the one-pair monadic Gödel representation reduces to endpoint-containing fixed-point subchains. For ordered B,C, lower commutation implies a regressive monotone idempotent product with fixed points exactly \(B\cap C\) and hence equals floor to \(B\cap C\). If a common gap contains both kinds of exclusive points, evaluation at the later point witnesses a strict composition inequality; without such a gap, both compositions round to the common left endpoint. Reversing order establishes the same criterion for upper maps. Four-letter words split uniquely at common fixed points, yielding the generating function 1/(1-4z+2z²), recurrence and closed form. The actual bundled verify.py checked all ordered subchain pairs through \(n=12\), composite identities, and an independent brute-force unary-map characterization for \(n\le4\); no finite test replaces the general proof.

value.rationale: Commutation among two independently selected monadic Gödel quantifier pairs is a motivated multi-agent compatibility property, and is not automatic from either structure individually. The result gives a sharp forbidden-gap normal form, an exact composite quantifier on the intersection subalgebra, an all-size ordered-pair census, and exponentially vanishing compatible proportion. The result is an intrinsic structural theorem about a natural logical object, not a mere new name for OEIS A007070 or the already known single-pair count.
